title: KĀLA-YANTRA v3 action record, run/actions/<action_id>.json (relaunch plan v2.7 §4a.1, §4a.6)
description: Written by kyaction.py before a side effect (state INTENDED: inputs, target identity, intended transition) and completed with the OBSERVED result after it (DONE or FAILED). A record is never overwritten by a second begin; a FAILED attempt reopened by retry is kept in attempts[]; every reconciliation of an unfinished record against real evidence is kept in reconciliations[]. A model job records its own side effects through `kyaction.py begin|complete|fail` as a job actor {role, holder_kind: job, controller_id, run_id}, only under ids JOB-<run_id>-<slug>; nobody else writes an id of that form. `process` is the pid and start identity of the process that began the record (null for a job's record and when it could not be read): it is what a second begin judges 'in_progress' from. Shape only: that the result was really observed, that inputs/target identify the action, that action_id equals the file name and that a job's id carries its own run id is not checked by this schema. Timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 ('Z' or '+00:00').

process.description: Who began (or, after a retry, reopened) the record. Optional: records written before B-0c rework 1, and by other writers, carry none.

attempts.description: Earlier FAILED attempts, oldest first (written by retry).

reconciliations.description: What real evidence said about an unfinished record. 'unknown' never completes it and never permits a retry; identical consecutive answers are counted, not repeated.

detail.description: The observer's evidence; any JSON value (an object when the outcome is done).

allOf.$comment: The JOB- namespace belongs to job actors, and a job actor writes nothing outside it.

actor.description: Who acts: the role, the kind of holder, and the holder's identity. Controller identity and provider-session identity are separate fields; at least one is present. A job actor is exactly {role, holder_kind: job, controller_id, run_id}: the controller that launched the job and the run the job belongs to.
